scenes.tts: Turn your head, and your eyes stay fixed on the world. How does the ear do that?
scenes.visual: A person turns their head while their gaze stays on a picture on the wall. Question on screen.
scenes.narration: Turn your head, and your eyes stay fixed on the world. How does the ear do that?

scenes.tts: Same switch, new front end. A semicircular canal is a fluid-filled ring.
scenes.visual: One hair cell from the earlier films, then a canal ring around it. Label: same switch, new front end.
scenes.narration: Same switch, new front end. A semicircular canal is a fluid-filled ring.

scenes.tts: In its swelling, hair bundles sit in a gelatinous flap called the cupula.
scenes.visual: Zoom into the canal's swelling, the ampulla: bundles embedded in a flap. Label: cupula.
scenes.narration: In its swelling, hair bundles sit in a gelatinous flap called the cupula.

scenes.tts: When the head turns, the fluid lags behind, bends the cupula, and pushes the bundles.
scenes.visual: The ring rotates; the fluid inside lags; the cupula bends; the bundles tip.
scenes.narration: When the head turns, the fluid lags behind, bends the cupula, and pushes the bundles.

scenes.tts: During everyday head movements, the canal's nerve fibres signal roughly how fast the head is turning.
scenes.visual: A head-velocity trace and a firing-rate trace rise and fall together. Label: roughly velocity.
scenes.narration: During everyday head movements, the canal's nerve fibres signal roughly how fast the head is turning.

scenes.tts: They fire even at rest. Canals on opposite sides pair up.
scenes.visual: Left and right horizontal canals drawn as a pair; both fibres show a steady resting spike train.
scenes.narration: They fire even at rest. Canals on opposite sides pair up.

scenes.tts: A turn to the left excites the left canal and inhibits the right.
scenes.visual: Head turns left: the left fibre's rate rises, the right fibre's rate falls. Label: push-pull.
scenes.narration: A turn to the left excites the left canal and inhibits the right.

scenes.tts: The canals drive the vestibulo-ocular reflex, which keeps the eyes still in the world.
scenes.visual: Label: vestibulo-ocular reflex (VOR). The circuit begins to draw.
scenes.narration: The canals drive the vestibulo-ocular reflex, which keeps the eyes still in the world.

scenes.tts: In a left turn, the left vestibular nucleus excites the right abducens nucleus.
scenes.visual: Step 1 lights: left horizontal canal to left vestibular nucleus to right abducens nucleus.
scenes.narration: In a left turn, the left vestibular nucleus excites the right abducens nucleus.

scenes.tts: It drives the right lateral rectus, and the right eye turns right.
scenes.visual: Step 2: right abducens to right lateral rectus; the right eye rotates rightward.
scenes.narration: It drives the right lateral rectus, and the right eye turns right.

scenes.tts: Abducens interneurons cross to the left oculomotor nucleus, which turns the left eye right.
scenes.visual: Step 3: an interneuron crosses and runs up the medial longitudinal fasciculus (MLF) to the left oculomotor nucleus, then the left medial rectus; the left eye rotates rightward.
scenes.narration: Abducens interneurons cross to the left oculomotor nucleus, which turns the left eye right.

scenes.tts: Both eyes turn right as the head turns left.
scenes.visual: Head turns left, both eyes turn right; the gaze stays on the picture.
scenes.narration: Both eyes turn right as the head turns left.

scenes.tts: Now the left inner ear is suddenly destroyed. The head is still. What does the brain think is happening?
scenes.visual: The left labyrinth greys out. The head is motionless. Question on screen.
scenes.narration: Now the left inner ear is suddenly destroyed. The head is still. What does the brain think is happening?

scenes.tts: The right side's resting firing is now unmatched. The brain reads a turn to the right.
scenes.visual: Left fibre silent, right fibre still firing at rest. A ghost arrow shows a rightward head turn.
scenes.narration: The right side's resting firing is now unmatched. The brain reads a turn to the right.

scenes.tts: The eyes drift slowly left, with quick jerks back to the right. The room seems to spin. That is one mechanism of vertigo.
scenes.visual: The eyes drift slowly left and flick back right, though the head is still; the room behind them spins. Label: one mechanism of vertigo.
scenes.narration: The eyes drift slowly left, with quick jerks back to the right. The room seems to spin. That is one mechanism of vertigo.

scenes.tts: The otolith organs sense gravity and straight-line acceleration. Their bundles are capped by a crystal-loaded membrane.
scenes.visual: The utricle, roughly horizontal, and the saccule, roughly vertical. Zoom: a gel membrane studded with calcium carbonate crystals on top of the bundles.
scenes.narration: The otolith organs sense gravity and straight-line acceleration. Their bundles are capped by a crystal-loaded membrane.

scenes.tts: Tilt the head back, and that heavy membrane slides backward.
scenes.visual: The head tilts back; the crystal-loaded membrane shears backward; the bundles bend.
scenes.narration: Tilt the head back, and that heavy membrane slides backward.

scenes.tts: Accelerate forward, as an aircraft does on its takeoff run, and it slides backward too. Without a view outside, you can feel tipped back.
scenes.visual: An aircraft accelerating down a runway; inside, the same backward shear of the membrane. A passenger in a windowless cabin feels tipped back.
scenes.narration: Accelerate forward, as an aircraft does on its takeoff run, and it slides backward too. Without a view outside, you can feel tipped back.

scenes.tts: So an otolith organ alone cannot tell tilt from acceleration. A tilt also rotates the head, and the canals feel rotation.
scenes.visual: Side by side: tilt and forward acceleration give the same shear. Only the tilt shows a canal signal, which separates them.
scenes.narration: So an otolith organ alone cannot tell tilt from acceleration. A tilt also rotates the head, and the canals feel rotation.

scenes.tts: One switch. A wave, a ring of fluid, a heavy membrane.
scenes.visual: The lesson's closing table builds row by row: cochlea, canals, otoliths, each with the same hair cell.
scenes.narration: One switch. A wave, a ring of fluid, a heavy membrane.

scenes.tts: And circuits that read which cells are active, and how the two sides compare.
scenes.visual: Final card: one switch; mechanics in front; circuits that read which cells and which side.
scenes.narration: And circuits that read which cells are active, and how the two sides compare.
